successors.name: Han dynasty
successors.text: Han took over the Old Chosŏn lands and established the Four Commanderies of Han in the western part of former Old Chosŏn

ledger.x: 197 BCE: Gojoseon enters the map under King Jun.
194 BCE: Wi Man overthrows King Jun and founds Wiman Joseon.
194 BCE: Wi Man makes Wanggeom-seong (Pyongyang) his capital.
109 BCE: Emperor Wu of Han invades Wiman Joseon.
108 BCE: Wanggeom falls and the fighting ends.
108 BCE: Han takes Old Chosŏn and sets up Lelang, Lintun and Zhenfan.
108 BCE: Wiman Joseon falls and Gojoseon ends.

wars.name: Han invasion of Wiman Joseon
wars.outcome: Han victory: Wanggeom fell in 108 BCE, Wiman Joseon ended and Han set up the commanderies of Lelang, Lintun and Zhenfan (108) and Xuantu (107).

certainty.note: No treaty or survey line on either page; the extent of Old Chosŏn is itself debated (the Gojoseon page notes the Manchurian scope favoured since the 1980s).
